title: FDA Issues Most Serious Recall for Tandem Mobi Insulin Pumps After 1,248 Serious Injuries
excerpt: The FDA has issued its most serious recall for Tandem Mobi insulin pumps after 1,248 serious injuries linked to false alarms that can stop insulin delivery.
content:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced its most serious type of recall — a Class I recall — for Tandem Mobi insulin pumps with Interoperable Technology, after Tandem Diabetes Care reported 1,248 serious injuries and no deaths associated with the issue as of Oct. 28, 2026.

The FDA announced the recall on Nov. 25, 2026. The pumps deliver insulin under the skin for diabetes management and can pair with continuous glucose monitors.

According to the FDA, certain pumps may generate false-positive occlusion alarms when no actual insulin flow obstruction exists. The pump then suspends insulin delivery until the user acknowledges the alarm and resumes therapy. Repeated false alarms can interrupt insulin delivery and raise blood glucose, in severe cases requiring medical intervention or hospitalization.

The cause, according to the FDA recall record, is increased friction in the pump's drive mechanism, which can slow the motor and which the pump misreads as a blockage.

About 80,938 devices are included in the recall, including about 78,000 in the United States.

What the FDA says to do

What the FDA says to do depends on the pump's serial number. Units on the replacement list should be returned and replaced immediately. Users can request a replacement through the link in Tandem's customer letter or by calling Tandem Customer Technical Support at 877-801-6901.

Units not on the replacement list can keep being used under updated use instructions, according to the FDA.

Tandem sent customer letters on Sept. 23, 2026. The FDA advises users to check their serial number against the FDA list and to contact Tandem or their clinician with questions.

Questions to watch

The FDA and Tandem have not stated in the recall information provided how many of the affected pumps are in use in Webb County or the Laredo area. It is also not stated how many replacement pumps have been requested so far. Webb Watch 956 will continue to follow the recall for local impact.
